To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pandemic has led to the emergence of new regional value chains in industries in which reliability is critical.
the disruption of the trade activities of MNEs as a consequence of Covid-19 has reinvigorating the debate on GVCs and the risks and challenges of offshoring.

the pandemic is likely to accelerate a trend toward a greater regional footprint in industries where resilience and reliability are important and that this shift is likely to affect the types of upgrading trajectory and the governance systems of value chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of COVID-19 on the governance of global value chains and the implications for regionalisation and reshoring.
the governance of global value chains and how this might be affected by the Covid 19 crisis.
how the pandemic is affecting the governance of GVCs and how it may affect their configuration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Covid 19 crisis has not changed the global value chains (or the world) in a fundamental way.
the Covid 19 crisis has accelerated a trend that was already under way: a more regional configuration of value chains.

the Covid 19 crisis has accelerated the trend toward regionalization of GVCs, but the extent and the pace of this change will depend on the type of industries and on the nature of the value activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the COVID-19 crisis is a wake-up call for the need to rethink the governance of global value chains, especially in those sectors in which resilience and supply chain security are critical.

the Covid 19 shock is likely to affect the governance of GVCs in two main ways: by increasing the importance of regionalization, and by increasing the need to address the challenges of resilience and reliability in GVCs.
the Covid 19 crisis has reinvigorates the debate about the risks and challenges of offshoring and the configuration of global supply chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Covid 19 crisis has created a new wave of regionalisation in global value chains, with important implications for the configuration of global production networks and the governance of value chains.
the pandemic is likely to accelerate regionalization in industries in which reliability and resilience are key.
the Covid 19 crisis is likely to accelerate a trend toward regionalization in GVCs.
